Energy transition

Rise of Renewables

Wind and solar are getting cheaper in California. Waiting could save you money, but new factories will need power before long.

Play Rise of Renewables↗ Your decisions ↓

Choose your difficulty before you start. It’s free to play in your browser.

Location
San Francisco, California
Starts in
2002
Your term
12 years

Your starting point

You take over a San Francisco utility in 2002 with nuclear and oil plants. Over your twelve-year term, gas plants get cheaper to build, followed by solar and wind projects.

The lower construction prices apply to new orders. If you wait for a discount, check how much time you'll have left to build before factory demand rises.

Learn how to play

Your decisions

  1. 01

    Choose when to order

    Check the forecast for equipment prices alongside the opening date for a new plant.

  2. 02

    Cover the evening peak

    Compare the hours your wind and solar projects produce power with the hours customers use it. What else needs to run then?

  3. 03

    Pay the bills while you build

    Until the new projects open, you're still paying for the oil your existing plant burns.

Which project would you order first?
